grh_59677cb766e0fc673baa.title: Mr Blandings Builds His Dream House
paragraphs: New York advertising executive Jim Blandings and his wife Muriel flee their cramped apartment for what looks like an idyllic Connecticut farmhouse, only to learn that the old house must be torn down and their affordable country dream rebuilt from scratch. Construction costs explode through rock blasting, a vanishing water supply, an endlessly deep well and one expensive surprise after another until Jim's planned $10,000 home becomes a roughly $48,000 ordeal. At the same time he is under pressure to invent a new slogan for the Wham Ham account. Household worker Gussie casually supplies the winning line, saving Jim's job, and after all the grief, debt and jealousy, Jim admits that if he had to do it over again he would still build the dream house.

This [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]] broadcast aired on June 9, 1950. It is listed as episode 72 in the archive. [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Cary Grant, Betsy Drake, and Hank Potter. Other credited names include Milton Geiger as radio adaptor and Jimmy Wallington as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.47c43e9eb0213c63|RCA]].
This version presents a radio version of [[work|work.sdp.film.633e354abf6ba91f|Mr Blandings Builds His Dream House]]. Milton Geiger adapted it for radio.

grh_591399d35d1752aa5c65.title: The Gunfighter
paragraphs: Notorious gunman Jimmy Ringo comes to town hoping for one quiet meeting with estranged wife Peggy and the young son who barely knows him. His reputation makes peace almost impossible: crowds gather, three brothers hunt him for revenge, and young would-be gunfighters dream of becoming famous by killing him. Marshal Mark Strett buys Jimmy enough time to see Peggy and arrange a possible future reunion, but as Ringo leaves, swaggering Hunt Bromley shoots him from ambush. Dying, Ringo falsely says he drew first so Bromley will escape the law, then condemns him to the same life he hated: forever watching for the next young gun who wants fame by killing the man who killed Jimmy Ringo.

[[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Gregory Peck, Wally Maher, Byron Kane, Ted de Corsia, and Sam Edwards. Other credited names include Bill Cairn as director, Nat Wolff as radio adaptor, and Jimmy Wallington as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 60 minutes.
This version presents a radio version of [[work|work.sdp.film.d27e8a1c3a7d09d0|The Gunfighter]]. Nat Wolff adapted it for radio.

grh_592305e11daf7447e012.title: Here's Morgan Once More
paragraphs: A Henry Morgan comedy revue made up of separate satirical sketches rather than one continuous story. Morgan and the cast move through jokes about children and television advertising, doctors chasing publicity with increasingly absurd medical claims, a mock continuing serial called Detergent, and a routine built around an adult-book shop, along with additional short comic pieces. The program relies on Morgan's dry delivery, wordplay and social satire, with each segment standing on its own instead of contributing to a single plot.

Other credited names include Fletcher Markle as director, Fletcher Markle as producer, Henry Morgan as writer, and Andy Griffith as host.
The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.9b0a0ccffce2f7d3|Sears, Roebuck and Company]].

grh_59157a0737ff7a597f78.title: Shrinking People
paragraphs: Explorer Peter Strensky learns that his wife Ellen plans to leave him for John and pretends to arrange a civilized divorce. Instead he poisons John, imprisons Ellen and uses a South American shrinking technique to turn both lovers’ bodies into doll-sized trophies for his lectures. Fleeing England with the preserved pair hidden in a trunk, Strensky begins hearing their voices, throws them overboard and is finally dragged into the sea by the tiny figures he thought he had destroyed.
